title: Corning Just Signed a Multibillion-Dollar Fiber Deal for AI and Broadband With Verizon. What That Means for GLW Stock.
excerpt: Corning’s latest multibillion-dollar fiber agreement with Verizon adds another major customer commitment as AI infrastructure drives demand for optical conne...
content_html:
Corning (GLW) is now home to another massive fiber deal. On Sept. 8, Verizon (VZ) struck a multibillion-dollar supply agreement with Corning for more than 80 million miles of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions through 2032. Fiber not only supports Verizon's broadband initiative but is needed for the construction of the long-haul, low-latency network necessary to link artificial intelligence (AI) data centers.

The timing is particularly fortuitous for Corning. The company already has a multibillion-dollar deal in place with Amazon (AMZN), as well as an initiative tied to Nvidia's (NVDA) AI infrastructure construction. Simply put, Corning is gaining traction in several different layers of the network, both inside and outside AI data centers.

About Corning Stock

Corning is a materials science corporation with its headquarters in Corning, New York. The company specializes in glass, ceramics, optical physics, and manufacturing. Corning offers its products in optical communications, mobile consumer electronics, displays, automotive, and other areas. Currently, Corning has a market capitalization of approximately $124 billion.

GLW stock currently trades near the $148 level. Although the stock is trading about 45% below its 52-week high of $271.78, shares still have appreciated about 70% year-to-date (YTD). This beats the S&P 500 Index ($SPX) over the same period, which has gained roughly 11% so far in 2026. GLW stock has also almost doubled from its 52-week low of $77.05.

All this performance leaves Corning with a tough valuation profile. GLW stock trades at about 43.7 times forward earnings and 7.9 times sales. But there are some fundamental reasons behind this valuation premium, because Corning recently won another big customer. Indeed, the new agreement with Verizon comes after a multibillion-dollar contract with Amazon. The company also has a partnership with Nvidia for the expansion of U.S. optical connectivity manufacturing capacity by 10 times and fiber production capacity by more than 50%.

Corning pays a quarterly dividend of $0.28 per share, providing a yield of roughly 0.8% at the latest share price. The next dividend payment will be made on Sept. 29 to shareholders of record on Aug. 31.
